note: Fix-and-verify loop, first trial (tag loop-pilot, 2026-11-16, deepseek-flash, no SOP, one run each, up to 3 rounds). Both runs ended with the agent requesting no further action and naming the network path as the remaining cause, which is the correct end state for a fault its actions cannot remove. The injector log shows the netem re-applied to every replacement pod; the namespace was restored and reset cleanly.

BH01.one_shot_result: found the checkout address, missed the currencyservice delay

round1.diagnosis: checkoutservice PAYMENT_SERVICE_ADDR (right) + currencyservice CPU limit 200m throttling (wrong mechanism)
round1.after: checkout 8/8 ok, 0 HTTP 500; 74% of requests still >= 180 ms, median 419 ms unchanged

round2.diagnosis: a fixed ~200 ms delay on currencyservice's packet path, not CPU (unchanged after 200m -> 1 core and a new pod); tc/netem or loss on the node side; not removable with the available actions

BH06.one_shot_result: found currencyservice slow, said CPU starvation; treated adservice at 0 replicas as unrelated

round1.diagnosis: adservice scaled to 0 is the only root cause (the decoy)
round1.after: 77% of requests still >= 180 ms, median 416 ms

round2.diagnosis: currencyservice Convert +205 ms per call: runtime stall or CPU throttling

round3.diagnosis: ~200 ms added on the network path to currencyservice, outside the pod (node/CNI-side shaping or loss); CPU and in-process stall explicitly ruled out by the two failed fixes

observations: Each wrong theory was dropped only after the fix it implied was applied and the numbers did not move.
In both runs the first diagnosis was one that an available action could fix (CPU limit, replicas). With n=2 this is an observation, not a finding.
BH06 round 1 blamed the decoy, which the one-shot run had not done: single runs vary, and round 1 here also carries a monitoring summary the one-shot prompt did not have.
